physicalNotes: Radius 0.27210324 Jupiter radii from Nicholson et al. 2024 (2024MNRAS.532.4632N), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024MNRAS.532.4632N/abstract): 19,453.2 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.03089718 Jupiter masses (Nicholson et al. 2024, the mass the NASA Exoplanet Archive's composite table adopts (2024MNRAS.532.4632N), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024MNRAS.532.4632N/abstract) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: ExoFOP, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname EXOFOP): P 11.62075439967 d
sources.shape: Nicholson et al. 2024 (2024MNRAS.532.4632N), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname NICHOLSON_ET_AL__2024): a/R* derived from its semi-major axis 0.1049 au and stellar radius 1.43 solar radii; Nicholson et al. 2024 (2024MNRAS.532.4632N), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname NICHOLSON_ET_AL__2024): inclination 89.26 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: ExoFOP, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname EXOFOP): transit mid-time 2458994.287456 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 18 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
